The present Dar arises out of road accident in which one Ravindra Das, aged about 33 years, suffered injuries. In terms of the provision of Motor Vehicle Act, the Ravindra Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21 Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83070665/ 1 same is treated as a claim petition. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 07.11.2021, upon receipt of information through Dd no. 41A regarding flipping of a vehicle near Khanna Market, Lodhi Road, investigating officer reached the spot where one vehicle Eicher Tempo bearing no. Dl-1Lae-4509 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) was found flipped on the middle of the road. The person injured had been taken to the hospital by then. On reaching the hospital, one of the injured Ganesh Das stated that on 07.11.2021 at 03:00 p.m., he was travelling along with 13 other people in the offending vehicle. After performing religious ritual (idol immersion) near Yamuna River, at Sarai Kale Khan, all the 13 passengers boarded the offending vehicle for returning to Bengali Camp. When the offending tempo reached near Najaf Khan Tomb, Najaf Khan Road, Lodhi Road, the driver of the offending vehicle /respondent no.1 started driving the vehicle at very high Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2024.10.21 04:15:58 +0530 Mact No. 332/22 Ravindra Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 04:18:05 Date: 2024.10.21 +0530 MACT No. 332/22 Ravindra Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 13 of 25(ss) physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 17. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Ravindra Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21 Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83070665/ 8 Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 17.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). CHARU by GUPTA GUPTA 2024.10.21 Date: 04:18:08 +0530 MACT No. 332/22 Ravindra Das vs. Akendra & 0rs. Page no. 14 of 25(ss) 17.2 . It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 17.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 17.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 17.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the Ravindra Das (Dar) vs Akendra Kumar (206/21 Lc) on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83070665/ 9 claimant. Decisions of Hon'ble SC and Hon'ble High Courts contain necessary guidelines for award under these heads, if necessary.
texts.facts: Police investigated the matter and filed chargesheet before concerned Criminal Court and Dar was filed before this Tribunal. 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1, is owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. In response to the Dar, insurance company filed its reply denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground that the offending vehicle was being plied in violation of the permit as per which the offending vehicle was only allowed to be use as a light goods carriage vehicle. It is further pleaded that even the injured Ravinder Das was found to be under influence of alcohol. It is pleaded that since the offending vehicle could be used only as a light goods carriage vehicle, petitioner was an unauthorized /gratuitous passenger along with 12 other persons, all of whom were in violation of the Covid-19 pandemic (Ddma guidelines) guidelines and thus not entitled to compensation. Despite opportunity, no reply was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 or respondent no.2. Opp. 3) Relief. 6. In the present case no separate evidence has been led by injured Ravindra Das , however, it is observed that a s per the report filed by Ld.LC, a common evidence has been recorded in all the 13 connected cases of victims as witnesses therein. 7. In respondent evidence, the driver of the offending vehicle /respondent no.1 as RW1 Akendra Kumar led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R1W1/A. In his examination in chief, he stated that the offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident. He denied any rash or negligent act on his part in driving of the offending vehicle. He stated that the petitioner/victims have falsely implicated him and that FIR no. 206/21 has been lodged with a motive to extort money from the respondents. Respondent no.2/ owner also examined himself as RW2/Sh. Bhanu Prakash Sharma. He led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R2WA and his identity card as Ex.R2W2/1. RW2 also denied involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident and pleaded the FIR to be false and concocted. He asserted that the liability to pay compensation, if any, lies upon the insurance company with which his vehicle was insured. 8. Insurance company /respondent no.3 also examined its witness Sh. Parth Arya as R3W1. R3W1 led his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/1 wherein he testified that as per the Registration Certificate, the offending vehicle was a light goods vehicle with a seating capacity of 3 persons. He is stated that the said vehicle was being used for transportation of passengers, beyond its permitted capacity, in violation of the permit. He testified that since the respondent no.1 and 2 committed breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by violating the RC and permit, the insurance company is not liable to compensate the petitioners. He relied upon his authority letter as Ex.R3W1/1, attested copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/3 and DAR /FIR /chargesheet/RC/Route Permit as already Ex.PW1/6 (colly). The court accordingly held that the insurance company shall have right to realize the compensation amount from the driver and owner of the vehicle in accordance with the law.
texts.arguments: It has been argued on behalf of the petitioner that since petitioner has suffered injury on account of accident that is proved to have occurred due to rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1, respondent no.3, with which the offending vehicle was insured, may be directed to compensate the petitioner. On the other hand, it is argued by respondent no.1 and 2 that the petitioner has failed to prove rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 or the involvement of the vehicle in the alleged accident. It is further argued that even if the accident is assumed to be proved, it is respondent no.3 which is liable to compensate the petitioner. It is argued on behalf of respondent no.3 that the petitioner/victims were traveling in the offending vehicle as unauthorized and gratuitous passengers since the offending vehicle was a goods carriage vehicle. It is argued that the offending vehicle was insured as a goods carriage vehicle and could not carry any passenger except for the driver and owner of the goods. It is further argued that the insured i.e. respondent no.2 has further violated the condition of RC which permitted a maximum of 3 persons to be seated in the offending vehicle. It is argued that as there is a clear breach of the terms and condition of the insurance policy, insurance company is not liable to compensate the victims. He has categorically stated that at the time of the accident, offending vehicle bearing no. DL-1LAE-4509 was being driven by Respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner. He has deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle deliberately ignored the warnings to be slow and careful. It is due to his rash and negligent driving that the offending vehicle overturned with the sudden and forceful impact causing injuries to its passengers and death of one of them.
